Terrorist: Donna, is the Wendigo ready?
Donna: It is. But it can only operate for 30 minutes.
Terrorist: Can you crush Incirlik Base in that time?
Donna: Yes. After that, do as you please.
Terrorist: Good. Today, here, we light the signal fire of our holy war.
Terrorist: And we shall warn the arrogant, complacent Federation Army, which dares to spread war with idols!
Donna: (Spreading war with idols... Not like I can talk.)
Kai: ...You didn't strike me as the violent type.
Donna: Don't move, Kai. ...You're right. I don't have any reason to be a terrorist.
Kai: Then what about them?
Donna: Put literally, they think it's blasphemous for <PT>s and <AM>s to be humanoid.
Donna: Well, best not to take them too seriously. Everyone considers them a bogus fringe group.
Donna: Maybe that's exactly why they accepted my offer, though.
Kai: And you are?
Donna: I've got nothing to do with it. I know there's no such thing as God.
Kai: You said you were at a military research lab?
Donna: To be precise, I wasn't military. I was on loan from a private company.
Donna: Man-machine interface R&D. Now that I think about it, that's where I heard your name back then...
Kai: You didn't know who I was when you approached me?
Donna: It was chance, honestly. I didn't know you were at this base until we met.
Donna: But you were right to worry about the supply theft incident. A veteran's sense, I suppose?
Kai: (...So that incident was...)
Kai: Your organization won't just stand by after something like this, will it?
Donna: Probably not. But I'm switching to a new patron. And before that, I need to show results.
Kai: ...What happens to me after this?
Donna: You'll be my hostage when I make my escape. Just in case.
Donna: So don't get any ideas. I don't want to make your wife and daughter cry.
Kai: They despise idol worship, don't they? They don't mind using your research over there?
Donna: This isn't a PT or an AM. It ended up a little warped and oversized... but it's my son's body.
Donna: It moves freely, just as I hoped... A sturdy body that can survive whether armies or aliens come.
Kai: ...You think you can crush a base with one machine? In 30 minutes, no less?
Donna: They want to see what I can do in that time. The target isn't so much the base as the PTs it sends out.
Donna: Besides... if I stay too long, I won't be able to get away, and I'll miss my ride out.
Kai: ...
Donna: Wait here, Kai Kitamura. I'll be right back.
Kai: ...
Kai: (Now then... I'm no child. I can't just sit here quietly and mind the house.)

Donna: ...Looks like our positions are reversed.
Kai: Yes... they are.
Donna: ...
Kai: You didn't strike me as the reckless type. ...Won't you tell me why?
Donna: I told you, didn't I? To prove the Wendigo's usefulness.
Kai: I mean your other reasons.
Donna: ...All right. After this, Tony and I won't get off lightly anyway...
Donna: So I'll tell you what I can while I still can. To you.
Kai: ...
Donna: The Tsentr Project, under way within the Federation Army... have you heard of it?
Kai: No. What is it?
Donna: A decade-ahead mass-production weapon program. The goal: autonomous units that need almost no maintenance.
Kai: ...Unmanned weapons that need no upkeep. Sounds like a pipe dream.
Donna: So did "an alien invasion." A few years ago, nobody thought that could ever become real.
Donna: Even after <DC> leader Dr. Bian Zoldark's speech, plenty of people couldn't believe it...
Donna: The <L5 Campaign> and <Inspector Incident> caused a paradigm shift, even among the Federation's brass.
Donna: Some of them seem to think PTs, AMs and Super Robots will hit a ceiling sooner or later.
Kai: ...And so this Tsentr Project was started.
Donna: Yes. But we were the ones who hit the ceiling first...
Donna: The targets were set so high that we struggled to get results. So I was taken off the project.
Kai: So... you switched sides?
Donna: Yes. For Tony's sake, I couldn't leave the Wendigo Plan.
Donna: But... it backfired, didn't it?
Kai: ...
Kai: ...An old comrade of mine is in Intelligence. I'll leave you and your son in his custody.
Kai: If you agree to a plea bargain, your sentence should be reduced somewhat.
Donna: But I did this on my own judgment.
Donna: And the Tsentr Project belongs to your own people... the Federation Army.
Donna: I don't know everything about it either. Even if you dig, you won't get to the truth.
Kai: What you've said is enough.
Donna: Heh... I won't get my hopes up about the treatment.
Kai: ...
Donna: Oh, right... I forgot to tell you the most important thing.
Kai: ?
Donna: Thank you, Kai. Maybe what Tony needed wasn't that body...
Donna: ...but someone to stop me.
Kai: ...
Donna: ...I'm in no position to say this, but... take good care of your wife and daughters.
Kai: Yeah...

Mitar: ...And so, the previous person in charge was handed over to Intelligence.
Erde: Won't that be a problem?
Mitar: Measures against leaks and the question of management responsibility are already taken care of.
Mitar: If anything, we're the victims. Donna Gallagher cost us a Wendigo, after all.
Erde: (...You destroyed yourself, Donna. Saved me the trouble.)
Mitar: Besides, the Tsentr Project isn't creating anything against the Federation Army's interests...
Mitar: We seek a way for humanity to survive the coming interstellar war. There's no cause to shut us down.
Erde: ...
Mitar: But our sponsors need interim results. ...This isn't charity work, after all.
Erde: And that's why you invited me here?
Mitar: Precisely. I want you to take over the Wendigo Plan.
Erde: ...I've read through the summary. If I had to single out one point of interest, it would be Wendigo 3's bone frame...
Erde: As for the man-machine interface, allow me to present an alternative proposal.
Mitar: ...Are you confident?
Erde: If I weren't, I wouldn't have accepted your invitation, Doctor.
Mitar: Very well. Proceed however you see fit.
Erde: Thank you. In that case, I'd like to change the plan's name.
Mitar: To what?
Erde: The "AI1 Plan"...
